deviation_tier.support: סעיף 1: ירושלים השלמה והמאוחדת היא בירת ישראל. | סעיף 3: המקומות הקדושים יהיו שמורים מפני חילול וכל פגיעה אחרת ומפני כל דבר העלול לפגוע בחופש הגישה של בני הדתות אל המקומות המקודשים להם או ברגשותיהם כלפי אותם המקומות.
deviation_tier.note: Coded on the 1980 text as enacted, which has ss. 1-4 only (ss. 5-7 were added later). Value engaged: core human rights and equality, in two opposite ways. (1) s. 1 declares 'complete and united' Jerusalem the capital; under the widened reading its foreseeable effect falls differently on Palestinians living under Israeli rule in the parts of the city brought under Israeli rule in 1967, through territory and political status. The departure is declaratory: s. 1 draws no boundary and directs no different treatment by group, so Limited, not Sharp. (2) s. 3 protects a right on its face (the holy places and free access to them for members of all religions), an entrenchment. Contradiction takes precedence over entrenchment, so Limited, not Entrenches. s. 2 (seat of the President, Knesset, Government and Supreme Court) and s. 4 (development, special resources, the capital grant approved by the Knesset Finance Committee) engage none of the five values on my reading; s. 4 benefits all residents and is not group-differential on its face. The 1980 text has no special-majority clause. Principal subject: the status of Jerusalem as Israel's unified capital (s. 1). Readings rejected: Entrenches, which would treat s. 1 as purely symbolic and so count only s. 3 (rejected because the widened reading counts indirect territorial and political-status effects); Sharp (rejected because nothing in the text authorizes or requires different treatment by national group).

direction.support: סעיף 1: ירושלים השלמה והמאוחדת היא בירת ישראל.
direction.note: Axes engaged: preferring Jewish identity over equal citizenship, under the widened reading (s. 1's indirect, group-differential effect on Palestinians in East Jerusalem through territory and political status): Illiberal. Minority rights, s. 3 (free access to holy places for members of all religions): Liberal. No women's-rights or judicial-review axis. Coded from the principal subject, s. 1: Illiberal. Close call: Neutral, reading s. 1 as a symbolic designation of the capital that names no group; rejected because the sheet counts indirect, group-differential effects.

deviation_tier.source: https://fs.knesset.gov.il/15/law/15_lsr_300277.pdf (the file archived at the listed web.archive.org capture, read at its original address because web.archive.org reset every connection; scanned page checked against its text layer, which misreads כולל as בולל); https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק-יסוד:_ירושלים_בירת_ישראל (current text, read via action=raw)
deviation_tier.support: סעיף 2 (הוספת סעיפים 5 עד 7): "5. תחום ירושלים כולל, לענין חוק־יסוד זה, בין השאר, את כל השטח המתואר בתוספת לאכרזה על הרחבת תחום עיריית ירושלים מיום כ' בסיון התשכ"ז (28 ביוני 1967), שניתנה לפי פקודת העיריות. 6. לא תועבר לגורם זר, מדיני או שלטוני, או לגורם זר אחר בדומה לכך, בין דרך קבע ובין לתקופה קצובה, כל סמכות המתייחסת לתחום ירושלים והנתונה על פי דין למדינת ישראל או לעיריית ירושלים. 7. אין לשנות את הוראות סעיפים 5 ו־6 אלא בחוק־יסוד שנתקבל ברוב של חברי הכנסת."
deviation_tier.note: What the amendment adds: a purpose clause (s. 1: to restrict changes to Jerusalem's area and to the application of Israeli law, jurisdiction and administration there, and to bar transfer of any governmental or municipal authority over the area to any body not acting under Israeli law); new s. 5 (Jerusalem's area includes the whole area of the 1967 extension of the municipal boundaries); new s. 6 (no authority over that area may pass to a foreign political or governmental body, permanently or for a fixed period); new s. 7 (ss. 5-6 may be changed only by a Basic Law passed by a majority of the Knesset members); and a savings clause (s. 3) for the 1994 law implementing the Interim Agreement and for any other law. Value engaged: core human rights and equality, under the widened reading. The foreseeable effect falls on Palestinians living under Israeli rule in the 1967 extension area, through territory and political status: ss. 5-6 fix that area inside Jerusalem and bar any transfer of authority over it to a non-Israeli body, and s. 7's special majority makes this harder to change, which the sheet counts. The departure is indirect: no provision names a national group or directs different treatment by group, so Limited, not Sharp. I read the limit on transferring authority as binding every organ of the state rather than moving power between branches, so I did not count separation of powers as engaged. Principal subject: the territorial definition of Jerusalem and the ban on transferring authority over it (ss. 5-6), entrenched by s. 7. Reading rejected: None, treating the amendment as a sovereignty and foreign-relations measure that names no right or group (rejected because the widened reading counts indirect territorial and political-status effects and their entrenchment).

direction.support: סעיף 1 (מטרה): חוק־יסוד זה בא לקבוע בחוק־יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל, הגבלה על שינוי שטח תחומה של ירושלים ועל שינוי בהחלת המשפט, השיפוט והמינהל של מדינת ישראל בתחום זה וכן בא לאסור על העברת כל סוג של סמכות, שלטונית או עירונית, המתייחסת לתחום ירושלים, לידי כל גוף שאינו פועל מכוח חוק של מדינת ישראל. | סעיף 2 (הוספת סעיפים 5 עד 7): "5. תחום ירושלים כולל, לענין חוק־יסוד זה, בין השאר, את כל השטח המתואר בתוספת לאכרזה על הרחבת תחום עיריית ירושלים מיום כ' בסיון התשכ"ז (28 ביוני 1967), שניתנה לפי פקודת העיריות. 6. לא תועבר לגורם זר, מדיני או שלטוני, או לגורם זר אחר בדומה לכך, בין דרך קבע ובין לתקופה קצובה, כל סמכות המתייחסת לתחום ירושלים והנתונה על פי דין למדינת ישראל או לעיריית ירושלים. 7. אין לשנות את הוראות סעיפים 5 ו־6 אלא בחוק־יסוד שנתקבל ברוב של חברי הכנסת."
direction.note: Axis engaged: preferring Jewish identity over equal citizenship, under the widened reading (indirect, group-differential effect on Palestinians in the 1967 extension area through territory and political status, entrenched by s. 7). No minority-rights, women's-rights or judicial-review axis on the face of the text; the savings clause (s. 3) adds nothing on any axis. Principal subject, as the purpose clause states it: restricting changes to Jerusalem's territory and barring transfer of authority over it. Coded Illiberal. Close call: Neutral, as a territorial and foreign-relations measure naming no group; rejected under the widened reading.

deviation_tier.support: סעיף 2 (תיקון סעיף 7): בסעיף 7 לחוק–היסוד, במקום "סעיפים 5 ו־6" יבוא "סעיף 6" ובמקום "ברוב של חברי הכנסת" יבוא "ברוב של שמונים חברי הכנסת; אין לשנות את הוראות סעיף זה אלא בחוק־יסוד שהתקבל ברוב של חברי הכנסת". | סעיף 1 (תיקון סעיף 6): בחוק־יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל (להלן - חוק–היסוד), בסעיף 6, במקום הסיפה החל במילים "לתחום ירושלים" יבוא "לתחום עיריית ירושלים, ובכלל זה השטח המתואר בתוספת לאכרזה על הרחבת תחום עיריית ירושלים מיום כ' בסיוון התשכ"ז (28 ביוני 1967), שניתנה לפי פקודת העיריות, והכול כפי שהיה בתוקף ביום תחילתו של חוק־יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל (תיקון מס' 2)".
deviation_tier.note: What the amendment changes: (1) s. 6's ban on transferring authority to a foreign body now covers the Jerusalem municipal area including the 1967 extension, as it stood on the day this amendment took effect, and the words confining it to authority 'vested by law in the State of Israel or the Jerusalem municipality' are dropped, so the ban reaches any authority relating to the area; (2) s. 7 now protects s. 6 alone, raises the majority needed to change it from a majority of the Knesset members to eighty members, and protects s. 7 itself by a majority of the members; s. 5 (the territorial definition) loses its protection. Value engaged: core human rights and equality, under the widened reading: the amendment widens, freezes and makes harder to change a provision whose foreseeable effect falls on Palestinians living under Israeli rule in East Jerusalem through territory and political status; the sheet counts such entrenchment expressly. The effect is indirect and no provision directs different treatment by national group, so Limited, not Sharp. Principal subject: the eighty-member majority for s. 6 (s. 2 of the amendment). Removing s. 5 from s. 7 loosens one territorial provision, but s. 6 no longer depends on s. 5's definition, so this does not offset the tightening. Readings rejected: None, treating the change as procedural (rejected because the sheet counts entrenchment of a group-differential provision); Entrenches (rejected because what is entrenched is the departure, not one of the five values).

direction.support: סעיף 2 (תיקון סעיף 7): בסעיף 7 לחוק–היסוד, במקום "סעיפים 5 ו־6" יבוא "סעיף 6" ובמקום "ברוב של חברי הכנסת" יבוא "ברוב של שמונים חברי הכנסת; אין לשנות את הוראות סעיף זה אלא בחוק־יסוד שהתקבל ברוב של חברי הכנסת".

No minority-rights, women's-rights or judicial-review axis on the text. Principal subject: the eighty-member majority for s. 6. Coded Illiberal. Close call: Neutral, treating a change of amendment majority as procedural housekeeping; rejected because the procedure here entrenches a provision with a group-differential territorial effect. The de-entrenchment of s. 5 points weakly the other way and is outweighed.

deviation_tier.support: סעיף 1 (הוספת סעיף 6א): "6א. לא תוקם בירושלים נציגות רשמית של מדינה זרה אלא אם כן היא נציגות דיפלומטית המואמנת למדינת ישראל; מדינת ישראל תעודד הקמת נציגויות דיפלומטיות כאמור."
deviation_tier.note: What the amendment adds: s. 6A, which bars any official representation of a foreign state in Jerusalem other than a diplomatic mission accredited to Israel, and directs Israel to encourage such missions. s. 6A is not covered by s. 7's special majorities, which protect s. 6 and s. 7 only. Value engaged: core human rights and equality, under the widened reading only. The text names no right or group, but its foreseeable effect is to exclude from Jerusalem any foreign official mission that is not accredited to Israel; that falls on Palestinians living under Israeli rule in the city, through political status, and not on Jewish citizens. The effect is indirect and the second clause is declaratory, so Limited, not Sharp. Principal subject: foreign official representation in Jerusalem. This was the closest call of the five. Reading rejected: None, treating s. 6A as a foreign-relations measure that engages none of the five values on its face. I rejected it because the sheet counts indirect political-status effects, but the coding rests on an inference about which missions the ban would reach, which the text does not state.

direction.support: סעיף 1 (הוספת סעיף 6א): "6א. לא תוקם בירושלים נציגות רשמית של מדינה זרה אלא אם כן היא נציגות דיפלומטית המואמנת למדינת ישראל; מדינת ישראל תעודד הקמת נציגויות דיפלומטיות כאמור."
direction.note: Axis engaged: preferring Jewish identity over equal citizenship, under the widened reading only (indirect, group-differential effect on the political status of Palestinians in Jerusalem). No minority-rights, women's-rights or judicial-review axis on the text. Principal subject: confining foreign official representation in Jerusalem to missions accredited to Israel. Coded Illiberal. Close call: Neutral, as foreign-relations housekeeping that names no group; rejected only because indirect, group-differential effects count under the widened reading.

deviation_tier.support: סעיף 7: המדינה רואה בפיתוח התיישבות יהודית ערך לאומי, ותפעל על מנת לעודד ולקדם הקמה וביסוס שלה. | סעיף 1(ג): מימוש הזכות להגדרה עצמית לאומית במדינת ישראל ייחודי לעם היהודי.
deviation_tier.note: Value engaged: core human rights and equality, through several provisions. s. 1(c) reserves the right of national self-determination in Israel to the Jewish people (a right reserved to one national group). s. 3 makes 'complete and united' Jerusalem the capital (territory, political status). s. 4 makes Hebrew the state language and gives Arabic a 'special status', its use in state institutions to be regulated by law (language); s. 4(c) preserves the status Arabic had in practice. s. 5 opens the state to Jewish immigration (a preference reserved to one group). s. 7 makes Jewish settlement a national value that the State shall act to encourage and promote (land and settlement, a preference by group). s. 10 makes the Sabbath and Jewish festivals the fixed rest days, with a right for non-Jews to keep their own (a right on its face, partly protective). s. 11 requires a majority of the Knesset members to change the law, an entrenchment the sheet counts. Sharp because s. 7 directly requires the State to act ('ותפעל') to promote settlement identified by national group, and s. 5 likewise directs a preference by group. No other of the five values is engaged on the text. Principal subject: the definition of Israel as the nation state of the Jewish people, with national self-determination unique to it (s. 1). Reading rejected: Limited, treating s. 7 as declaratory ('a national value', 'encourage') and s. 1(c) as a statement of identity; rejected because s. 7's operative clause requires state action keyed to one national group.

direction.support: סעיף 1(ב): מדינת ישראל היא מדינת הלאום של העם היהודי, שבה הוא מממש את זכותו הטבעית, התרבותית, הדתית וההיסטורית להגדרה עצמית. | סעיף 1(ג): מימוש הזכות להגדרה עצמית לאומית במדינת ישראל ייחודי לעם היהודי.
direction.note: Axes engaged: preferring Jewish identity over equal citizenship (ss. 1, 3, 5, 7 and 11, directly and under the widened reading; s. 6 on ties with the Jewish people abroad more weakly): Illiberal. Minority rights, s. 4 (Arabic placed below Hebrew, its use left to statute): Illiberal, partly offset by s. 4(c). s. 10's right of non-Jews to keep their own rest days is the one Liberal element. No women's-rights or judicial-review axis. Principal subject: s. 1, the Jewish nation-state definition and exclusive national self-determination. Coded Illiberal; not a close call.
